Independently inspect this unmasked satellite image for agricultural field parcels and apparent residue burning. You are not given another model's class or confidence. A candidate region to assess is nominated only by these local pixel-edge polygon coordinates: [[500,332],[492,340],[492,456],[504,468],[508,448],[512,448],[512,408],[508,408],[512,352],[508,352],[508,336]]. Do not assume this candidate is a field or a burn. First state in your summary: "CANDIDATE: <burned-looking | partially burned-looking | unburned-looking | uncertain | not-a-field>." Follow with concise visual evidence, plausible alternatives, and whether the proposal traces a whole parcel or merely a patch. Darkness or a tan/white patch alone is insufficient evidence of burning. Burned-looking needs coherent char/ash-like appearance; partially burned-looking needs clear burn-like patches and other cover within the same parcel. Preserve uncertainty between soil, moisture, shadow, residue, and char. Do not infer season, location, crop species, activity date, fire event, severity, or calibrated confidence.
Then segment ALL major visible field parcels in this 1024x1024 image as provisional dataset additions. Typically 15–40 regions; include fewer or up to 70 when justified. Use class labels exactly: burned-looking field; partially burned-looking field; unburned-looking field; uncertain field; non-field confounder. Trace whole visible parcels independently of the nominated patch; do not force its outline to be correct. Label a salient non-field candidate separately when necessary, otherwise leave buildings and roads unlabeled. Avoid merging adjacent parcels, bounding rectangles across boundaries, overlaps, and holes unless required. Use 4–16 ordered vertices per parcel; mark image-edge fragments partial. Each note MUST start TAGS: followed by 3–6 lowercase comma-separated visible-appearance tags; then one or two evidence sentences. Add candidate-overlap to any parcel containing a substantial part of the nominated candidate. Include useful confounders and no-burn examples. These are model proposals for expert review, not human ground truth. Return valid JSON under the supplied schema.

Answer the user's visual question through the summary and requested objects. Omit objects that are absent, and explain uncertainty or ambiguity in warnings. Never infer pollution concentration, temperature, disease, identity, or physical area from an uncalibrated photograph. Label only visually supported objects or regions.
